methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pipedream is a Series A transportation company founded by Garrett McCurrach and Canon Reeves. The company has raised $22.4M to date. The transportation sector includes eight private comparables (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, FleetZero, Parallel Systems, and others) and no public peers.

Stage-progression methodology applies here, using the $22.4M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding $44.8M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while three same-sector transportation peers exist in the broader dataset, none meet minimum thresholds for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparability with sufficient sample size (≥3 datapoints), and extrapolating from all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given the sector's capital intensity and heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $38M (low) to $52M (high), with a median of $45M. This range reflects the stage-progression result and a conservative bandwidth around it. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-stage peer multiples in transportation, which limits cross-validation, and the inherent variation in Series A to growth-stage step-ups across transportation subsectors. Capital requirements and path-to-exit profiles likely differ materially across the peer set. A second valuation method anchored to comparable Series A financials or forward revenue multiples would strengthen conviction.
